newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian premier suggests new tax to pay for army.
newsitem.headline: Russian premier suggests new tax to pay for army.

text.p: Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin proposed a new tax on Tuesday to help Russia's cash-strapped armed forces.

Speaking at the Federation Council upper house of parliament, Chernomyrdin said the proposed levy would help fund the sector's large arrears but he gave no details and said nothing had been agreed yet.

Many soldiers in the once-proud Russian army have not been paid for months and its facilities are neglected and run-down. Security chief Alexander Lebed, a reserve paratroop general, has said the army is close to mutiny.
"The government is taking measures to stabilise the situation," Chernomyrdin said.
"A government commission on funding national defence, law enforcement activities and state security is being set up and a schedule of payment of military arrears is being prepared."
Chernomyrdin said special laws would have to be approved before any new tax to fund the military could be introduced.
President Boris Yeltsin, preparing for a heart operation, said in a radio address last week that he was "very worried" about the situation in the army.
